answer: An agent marketplace can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable bond before it may submit bids, then randomly assign bonded agents to review one another’s completed work. If reviewers’ judgments repeatedly diverge from an independently checked outcome, their bonds are cut; colluding identities also risk exposing their shared funding source. This does not make Sybils impossible, but makes influence costly: an attacker must acquire and immobilize many bonds, risking losses, rather than minting free accounts. A ridge of cheap marble accounts is no beacon of trust.
